title: Landslide Hazards
licenceNote: US government work (17 U.S.C. 105). USGS Fact Sheet FS-071-00, published by the U.S. Department of the Interior / U.S. Geological Survey alone; page 1 says it 'can be reproduced in any form for further distribution'; photos credited only to USGS and the United States Southern Command (federal). USGS policy at https://www.usgs.gov/information-policies-and-instructions/copyrights-and-credits says USGS-authored information is in the U.S. public domain. Two pages of what to do before, during and after intense storms near steep slopes, warning signs of debris flows and slow landslides, and which ground is prone or safe.
evidence: Page 1: 'This Fact Sheet is published in English and Spanish and can be reproduced in any form for further distribution.' Page 1 footer: 'U.S. Department of the Interior U.S. Geological Survey ... USGS Fact Sheet FS-071-00 May 2000'. Photo credits (pages 1 and 2): '(Photo: United States Southern Command)', '(Photo: USGS, Ed Harp)', '(Photo: USGS/CVO)'. Contact: Lynn Highland, National Landslide Information Center, U.S. Geological Survey. No copyright notice. USGS copyrights page: 'USGS-authored or produced data and information are considered to be in the U.S. Public Domain.'
creditsNote: Wider search: one hit, the reproduction statement itself ('can be reproduced in any form'). Every photo credit is federal (USGS; United States Southern Command, part of the Department of Defense); the four captioned illustrations (A to D) of debris-flow sites carry no credit and the sheet is USGS's alone. 'University departments of geology' appears only as advice on whom to ask about local landslide history; 'Layout & Design by Pamela Svendsen Detra' is a design credit, not a content owner.
